chunks: All that, its evil was odious to your Lord.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the evil of the deeds mentioned in the Night Journey?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Al-Isra, this verse serves as a concluding emphasis on the divine displeasure (makruhan) toward the specific prohibitions previously enumerated, such as shirk and injustice. Shia exegetes highlight that 'makruhan' implies a deep, intrinsic aversion from the Lord, reinforcing the weight of these moral and theological boundaries. It acts as a divine seal on the chapter's legal and ethical rulings, ensuring the believer understands the gravity of these transgressions.
